correctness.rationale: PASS: The covariance determinant identity and eigenvalue AGM prove the exact ball-simplex bound and classify equality. For the low-width branch, the explicit ellipsoid dominates every horizontal spherical-slab section by \(A(1-z^2/B)-(1-z^2)=(1-dt^2)(1-z^2/t^2)/(d-1)\ge0\). The determinant of its scaling gives the precise upper coefficient. Two orthogonal, centered k-simplices at opposite slab rims map to a regular d-simplex, attaining the upper bound for every odd d; the witness at the transition stays feasible for thicker slabs. Equality rigidity follows from the ball-simplex Gram condition, contact only at the two rims before the transition, balanced vertical signs, and forced orthogonal blocks. The occupied-volume ratio decreases strictly by an elementary integral-ratio argument. The standalone pure-Python verifier checked 12 rational parameter/dimension Gram determinants, six transition identities and four exact rational monotonicity sequences; the universal proof does not depend on sampling. No assertion is made for even dimensions.

value.rationale: PASS: The problem asks a natural extremal invariant of a continuous family interpolating between a thin Euclidean spherical slice and the unit ball. The sharp algebraic volume profile is given for every odd dimension, with a nontrivial saturation transition exactly at reciprocal square-root dimension, complete contact/equality classification, and a strictly decreasing occupied-volume fraction. These results are not a numerical recalculation of the regular ball simplex: the two-rim constraint creates a new, parity-dependent optimizer and a different volume law.
